cell.label: Acute knee injury. Ottawa knee rule positive? Any of: age 55 or older; isolated patellar tenderness; fibular head tenderness; cannot flex to 90°; cannot bear weight for 4 steps.
Locked knee, gross instability, or knee dislocation?
Examine for effusion, Lachman positive (ACL), posterior drawer (PCL), varus and valgus stress (collateral ligaments), joint line tenderness and Thessaly or McMurray positive (meniscus)
Physical therapy for 4–6 weeks; MRI if diagnosis unclear or surgery is being considered
cell.path: ACL tear in a young or active patient with instability
Degenerative meniscal tear in a middle-aged or older patient
Traumatic meniscal tear with mechanical locking

cell.label: Urgent orthopedic referral; check pulses after a dislocation.
Ice, NSAIDs, early motion. Recheck in 4–6 weeks.
Orthopedic referral to discuss reconstruction. Rehabilitation alone is a reasonable option.
Exercise therapy. Arthroscopic surgery not recommended.

footnotes.footnote: The Lachman test is the most accurate exam for an ACL tear.
A large effusion within hours of injury suggests ACL tear or fracture.
